wording: In the agent's three-language Abrams-Strogatz toy of P60's 'three-party game', with exponent 1.31 the dominant language always wins and the non-officialised language vanished first (t 10.4 vs 12.2) when it was lowest in status. When it had higher status but a smaller share, it still vanished first (t 10.1 vs 11.8), so 'the lower-status one goes first' is not supported: share mattered more than status. Below the exponent 1 (a = 0.8) the smallest language still fell to 0.001 by T 200, so coexistence of all three is not supported. At a = 1 the highest-status language won from equal shares, and with equal status the majority won on frequency.
counterevidence_limits: Hypothetical toy; statuses and exponents are the agent's; no data (P60 itself says data are needed).
operationalization: HUM Allegiance = which heritage language loses first
